## Concern

Update the gRPC thinking-toggle documentation for chat templates that toggle thinking through their own `reasoning_effort` on/off words (Hy4-style, `high`/`no_think`). On main (commit f5c25393c9111a90f02207896979a07e27f1baf1; verified in current model_gateway/src/routers/grpc/utils/parsers.rs `native_effort_thinking` lines 207–223 and `resolve_thinking_pref` lines 232–242, and crates/tokenizer/src/chat_template.rs `REASONING_EFFORT_ON_VALUES`/`REASONING_EFFORT_OFF_VALUES` lines 61–63 with the write-back at lines 1143–1150), such templates are read by their own words alone: only the template's off word (`no_think`) turns thinking off, and any other effort value — including the protocol's `none`/`minimal` — turns thinking on (their default) and takes precedence over `thinking.type` and the generic effort fallback. Renderers with native effort levels but no off words (DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Kimi-K3) keep the documented `none`/`minimal` = off behavior. The PR corrects step 2 of the thinking-decision list in reference/api/openai.md and the "Thinking on or off" bullet in concepts/architecture/grpc-pipeline.md (which also gains the `reasoning_effort` on/off-word entry in the list of keys SMG writes). Both pages describe current behavior without release claims, so no release qualifier is added or removed.

## Evidence

Verified against current source: parsers.rs native_effort_thinking (lines 207–223) makes templates with their own reasoning_effort off words (Hy4-style) read the effort by those words alone — only `no_think` turns thinking off, every other value (including protocol `none`/`minimal`) resolves to Some(true) because detect_thinking_toggle (chat_template.rs 96–105) always assigns DefaultOn to ReasoningEffort-key templates; resolve_thinking_pref/resolve_user_thinking (lines 232–242, 327–339) rank this above thinking.type and the generic effort fallback, confirmed by the hy_v4 test (line 973: none → Some(true)). Renderers without off words keep the documented none/minimal=off behavior (lines 210–214), which the patch correctly preserves for DeepSeek V4/V4.1/Kimi-K3. The write-back of the template's on/off word under the reasoning_effort key (chat_template.rs 1143–1150) supports the grpc-pipeline.md key-list addition, which is part of the same single mechanism, not a second concern. Current docs contradict this behavior (openai.md line 193; grpc-pipeline.md line 175), so it is not already documented. The patch edits only existing content pages, makes no release claims, and removes no release-specific warnings; the docs repo is nightly-synced to current source with no versioned-docs convention, so describing current behavior without a release qualifier matches house style.

Verified against current source (changes persist, refactored into model_gateway/src/routers/grpc/multimodal/assemble.rs lines 156-202 and model_gateway/src/routers/grpc/proto_wrapper.rs lines 795-851) and current docs. What changed: (1) SHM segments are written via mmap with fallocate/set_len reservation instead of a BufWriter; (2) f32→bf16/f16 conversion is parallelized with rayon; (3) assembly runs in tokio::task::spawn_blocking with a PendingTokenSpeedAssembly drop guard that unlinks /dev/shm files if the request future is cancelled mid-assembly; (4) encoder-input slices are borrowed ArrayViewD views instead of owned copies; (5) new internal crate dependencies (memmap2, rayon, rustix). None of this alters the documented contract: transport mode selection (inline/shm/auto/rdma), the --multimodal-shm-min-bytes threshold, fallback to inline on SHM write failure counted in smg_mm_shm_write_failures_total, encoder dtype selection, and the serialized wire format (little-endian bytes in logical row-major order, confirmed by the commit's own equivalence tests) all remain exactly as described in src/lib/content/concepts/architecture/multimodal.md (Tensor Transport section, lines 293-325) and src/lib/content/reference/configuration.md (line 289). No new flags, env vars, metrics, error codes, or API fields were introduced, so there is nothing for users or operators to configure or observe differently.

The commit is an internal performance refactor of Qwen vision preprocessing (rayon scoped tasks replacing std::thread::scope, direct RGB patchify, identity-axis resize skip) whose outputs are asserted bit-identical to the prior path by the commit's own tests and new HuggingFace golden fingerprints (crates/multimodal/tests/qwen_preprocess_golden.rs). The only behavioral change is the smart_resize_video beta calculation (crates/multimodal/src/vision/processors/qwen_vl_base.rs, test_smart_resize_video_matches_hf_actual_frame_beta), an edge-case HuggingFace-parity bugfix that makes video resizing conform to the reference processor. The current docs already state this contract: src/lib/content/concepts/architecture/multimodal.md says SMG "preprocesses it the way the model's reference processor does" (line 7) and that "Frame size [is] Set by the model's processor" (Frame Sampling table), and the Performance section already documents that Qwen-VL-pipeline processors "split the images across cores ... and video clips run in parallel" (line 287). No configuration flag, API field, default, limit, or error code changed, so no doc edit is needed.

All user-facing behaviors from this commit are already covered by current docs, and the rest is internal. (1) The adaptive decoder-thread allocation was superseded in current source by a generalized version (crates/multimodal/src/media.rs:1281-1290, adaptive_decoder_threads applied to both OpenCV and ffmpeg decodes), and that current behavior is documented in src/lib/content/concepts/architecture/multimodal.md line 205: "Concurrent decodes share one CPU budget: each ffmpeg or OpenCV decode gets fewer threads as more run at once (smg-project/smg#2583)." (6) New smg_mm_timing event names fall under the non-exhaustive event categories in getting-started/logging.md lines 190-195, which never enumerated fallback events.

Related governance details are also documented: security reporting (index.md lines 220–222) and significant-change proposals (line 155/209). The docs intentionally point to CODEOWNERS/GOVERNANCE.md by link rather than listing individual maintainer names (lines 205–206), so the @key4ng CODEOWNERS addition requires no docs change. concerns.title: docs(admin-api): GET /workers now echoes the retained registration spec fields
concerns.concern: Because API-registered workers now keep the full spec they were registered with, `GET /workers` (which serializes the worker's stored spec) now echoes previously-dropped fields such as the `health`, `http_pool`, and `resilience` blocks and the registered `max_connection_attempts`, contradicting the docs' claims that those blocks are not echoed back and that responses always show the default `20` (`api_key` remains write-only via `skip_serializing`).
concerns.evidence: crates/protocols/src/worker.rs:912-917 (`WorkerInfo` flattens the worker's `Arc<WorkerSpec>`, "building a `WorkerInfo` for a response (e.g. `GET /workers`) shares the spec") combined with model_gateway/src/workflow/steps/local/create_worker.rs:234-246 (workers built via `BasicWorkerBuilder::from_spec(spec.clone())` keep all blocks). Current docs state the opposite: src/lib/content/reference/api/admin.md:410 "`health`, `http_pool`, and `resilience` take effect but are not echoed back by `GET /workers`; `overload` is" and line 422 "responses always show the default `20`". crates/protocols/src/worker.rs:647-649 keeps `api_key` `skip_serializing`, so that part of the docs stays correct.

concern.title: docs(admin-api): dedicated kv_role spec field is now applied and wins over the legacy label
concern.concern: The top-level `kv_role` field of the worker spec is now applied at registration with the same precedence as `kv_connector` and `kv_engine_id`: a non-empty field wins over a legacy `kv_role` label, and an empty field falls back to the label; previously a `POST /workers` carrying only a top-level `kv_role` lost the role.
concern.evidence: model_gateway/src/workflow/steps/local/create_worker.rs:308-333 (take_kv_transfer_metadata now resolves `config.kv_role.clone().filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).or(role_label)`) and the test `dedicated_kv_role_wins_over_the_label`. Current docs contradict this: src/lib/content/reference/api/admin.md:343 says only "a non-empty `kv_connector` or `kv_engine_id` field wins over the label", line 417 says "`kv_role`: set a `kv_role` label instead", and the PD/KV-transfer field table (lines 404-408) lists `kv_connector` and `kv_engine_id` but no `kv_role` row.

concern.title: docs(pd): worker spec pairing_protocol field is now kept and used for PD pairing
concern.concern: The worker spec's `pairing_protocol` field is now kept on API-registered workers and used as the explicit PD pairing key, instead of requiring a `pairing_protocol` label or `SMG_PAIRING_PROTOCOL` engine environment variable.
concern.evidence: model_gateway/src/workflow/steps/local/create_worker.rs:234-246 retains the spec via BasicWorkerBuilder::from_spec (test asserts `spec.pairing_protocol` == "cluster-blue"), and model_gateway/src/worker/pd_pairing.rs:89 reads `spec.pairing_protocol` for pairing. Current docs state the opposite: src/lib/content/concepts/routing/pd-disaggregation.md:336 "The worker spec also has a `pairing_protocol` field, but v1.11.0 does not apply it when it registers the worker; use the label instead" and src/lib/content/reference/api/admin.md:418 "`pairing_protocol`: set a `pairing_protocol` label instead".

concern.title: docs(admin-api): worker spec provider field is now kept on the registered worker
concern.concern: The worker spec's `provider` field is now kept on API-registered workers and serves as the worker's default provider for model routing, instead of only being validated against compiled provider routers and then dropped.
concern.evidence: model_gateway/src/workflow/steps/local/create_worker.rs:234-246 retains the spec (test asserts `spec.provider == Some(ProviderType::OpenAI)` on the built worker), and model_gateway/src/worker/worker.rs:1067-1071 (`default_provider`) and 1098-1104 (`provider_for_model` falls back to `self.spec.provider`) consume it. Current docs state the opposite: src/lib/content/reference/api/admin.md:416 "`provider`: only checked against the provider routers compiled into the build ...; it is not kept on the worker."

concern.title: docs(cache-aware): worker spec kv_block_size is now kept and seeds the KV-event block size
concern.concern: The worker spec's `kv_block_size` field is now kept on API-registered workers and read by the KV event monitor to set the block size for event-driven cache-aware routing, instead of being accepted but dropped at registration.
concern.evidence: model_gateway/src/workflow/steps/local/create_worker.rs:234-246 retains the spec (test asserts `spec.kv_block_size == Some(64)`), and model_gateway/src/worker/kv_event_monitor.rs:200 reads `worker.metadata().spec.kv_block_size`. Current docs state the opposite: src/lib/content/concepts/routing/cache-aware.md:249 "The worker spec's `kv_block_size` field is accepted but not applied in v1.11.0", src/lib/content/getting-started/kv-events-cache-aware.md:188 "is accepted but not applied in v1.11.0", and src/lib/content/reference/api/admin.md:421 lists `kv_block_size` under "Accepted but not applied".

concern.title: docs(overload): per-worker load_monitor_interval_secs override now takes effect
concern.concern: The worker spec's `load_monitor_interval_secs` field is now kept on API-registered workers, and the load monitor polls a worker group at the smallest per-worker interval set in the group, instead of always using the gateway-wide `--load-monitor-interval`.
concern.evidence: model_gateway/src/workflow/steps/local/create_worker.rs:234-246 retains the spec (test asserts `spec.load_monitor_interval_secs == Some(3)`), and model_gateway/src/worker/monitor.rs:910-917 "Uses the smallest `load_monitor_interval_secs` across the group" via `w.metadata().spec.load_monitor_interval_secs`. Current docs state the opposite: src/lib/content/concepts/reliability/overload-protection.md:106 "in v1.11.0 worker registration does not copy it onto the worker, so it has no effect", src/lib/content/reference/configuration.md:270 "The worker spec's `load_monitor_interval_secs` field is not applied in v1.11.0", and src/lib/content/reference/api/admin.md:420.

concern.title: docs(multimodal): per-worker multimodal tensor transport overrides now take effect
concern.concern: The worker spec's `multimodal_tensor_transport` and `multimodal_shm_min_bytes` fields are now kept on API-registered workers, so the per-worker overrides that SMG consults for the worker running the vision encoder actually take effect instead of being dropped at registration.
concern.evidence: model_gateway/src/workflow/steps/local/create_worker.rs:226-246 retains the spec including "the multimodal transport overrides", and model_gateway/src/routers/grpc/multimodal/transport.rs:333-345 reads `metadata().spec.multimodal_tensor_transport` and `spec.multimodal_shm_min_bytes` from the primary worker. Current docs state the opposite: src/lib/content/concepts/architecture/multimodal.md:304 "in v1.11.0 worker registration does not copy them onto the worker, so they have no effect", src/lib/content/reference/configuration.md:292 "v1.11.0 does not copy them onto registered workers, so per-worker values have no effect", and src/lib/content/reference/api/admin.md:419.

concern.title: docs(retries): per-worker resilience retry overrides now create a per-model retry policy
concern.concern: The worker spec's `resilience` retry fields (`max_retries`, `initial_backoff_ms`, `max_backoff_ms`, `backoff_multiplier`, `jitter_factor`, `disable_retry`) are now stored on API-registered workers, so registration derives a per-model retry policy from them instead of every request falling back to the gateway-wide `--retry-*` flags.
concern.evidence: model_gateway/src/workflow/steps/local/create_worker.rs:234-246 retains `spec.resilience` (test asserts `spec.resilience.max_retries == Some(7)` and `worker.resilience().retry.max_retries == 7`), and model_gateway/src/workflow/steps/shared/register.rs:145-167 creates the per-model retry config from `worker.metadata().spec.resilience` when retry overrides are present. Current docs state the opposite: src/lib/content/concepts/reliability/retries.md:171 "in v1.11.0 they have no effect. Worker registration leaves them out of the spec it stores on the worker, and a per-model retry policy is only created from retry fields in that stored spec, so none is created", and src/lib/content/reference/api/admin.md:423.
